pairs: Orta autem fame super terram post eam sterilitatem,
Then, when a famine arose over the land,
after that barrenness which had happened in the days of Abraham,
abiit Isaac ad Abimelech regem Palæstinorum in Gerara.
Isaac went to Abimelech, king of the Palestinians, in Gerar.
And the Lord appeared to him,
sed quiesce in terra quam dixero tibi,
but rest in the land that I will tell you,
and I will be with you,
tibi enim et semini tuo dabo universas regiones has,
For to you and to your offspring I will give all these regions,
complens juramentum quod spopondi Abraham patri tuo.
completing the oath that I promised to Abraham your father.
Et multiplicabo semen tuum sicut stellas cæli:
And I will multiply your offspring like the stars of heaven.
daboque posteris tuis universas regiones has:
And I will give to your posterity all these regions.
et benedicentur in semine tuo omnes gentes terræ,
And in your offspring all the nations of the earth will be blessed,
eo quod obedierit Abraham voci meæ,
et custodierit præcepta et mandata mea,
and kept my precepts and commandments,
and observed the ceremonies and the laws.”
And so Isaac remained in Gerar.
Qui cum interrogaretur a viris loci illius super uxore sua,
And when he was questioned by the men of that place about his wife,
timuerat enim confiteri quod sibi esset sociata conjugio,
For he was afraid to confess her to be his mate,
reputans ne forte interficerent eum propter illius pulchritudinem.
thinking that perhaps they would put him to death because of her beauty.
Cumque pertransissent dies plurimi, et ibidem moraretur,
And when very many days had passed, and he had remained in the same place,
prospiciens Abimelech rex Palæstinorum per fenestram,
Abimelech, king of the Palestinians, gazing through a window,
vidit eum jocantem cum Rebecca uxore sua.
saw him being playful with Rebekah, his wife.
Perspicuum est quod uxor tua sit:
“It is clear that she is your wife.
cur mentitus es eam sororem tuam esse?
Why did you falsely claim her to be your sister?”
“I was afraid, lest I might die because of her.”
potuit coire quispiam de populo cum uxore tua,
Someone from the people could have lain with your wife,
et induxeras super nos grande peccatum.
and you would have brought a great sin upon us.”
And he instructed all the people,
Qui tetigerit hominis hujus uxorem, morte morietur.
“Whoever will touch the wife of this man will die a death.”
Sevit autem Isaac in terra illa,
Then Isaac sowed in that land, and he found,
et invenit in ipso anno centuplum:
in that same year, one hundredfold.
and he continued prospering as well as increasing,
habuit quoque possessiones ovium et armentorum,
Likewise, he had possessions of sheep and of herds,
Because of this, the Palestinians envied him,
quos foderant servi patris illius Abraham,
they obstructed all the wells that the servants of his father Abraham had dug,
in tantum, ut ipse Abimelech diceret ad Isaac:
It reached a point where Abimelech himself said to Isaac,
quoniam potentior nobis factus es valde.
for you have become very much more powerful than we.”
he then went toward the torrent of Gerar,
Again, he dug up other wells,
quos foderant servi patris sui Abraham,
which the servants of his father Abraham had dug,
appellavitque eos eisdem nominibus quibus ante pater vocaverat.
And he called them by the same names that his father had called them before.
And they dug in the torrent,
But in that place also the shepherds of Gerar argued against the shepherds of Isaac,
et ibi jurgium fuit pastorum Geraræ adversus pastores Isaac,
quam ob rem nomen putei ex eo,
he called the name of the well,
Then they dug up yet another one.
And over that one also they fought,
et pro illo quoque rixati sunt,
Advancing from there, he dug another well,
over which they did not contend.
And so he called its name, ‘Latitude,’
Nunc dilatavit nos Dominus, et fecit crescere super terram.
“Now the Lord has expanded us and caused us to increase across the land.”
Ascendit autem ex illo loco in Bersabee,
Then he ascended from that place into Beersheba,
ubi apparuit ei Dominus in ipsa nocte,
where the Lord appeared to him on the same night,
Ego sum Deus Abraham patris tui:
“I am the God of Abraham your father.
et multiplicabo semen tuum propter servum meum Abraham.
and I will multiply your offspring because of my servant Abraham.”
And so he built an altar there.
And he invoked the name of the Lord,
and he stretched out his tent.
præcepitque servis suis ut foderent puteum.
And he instructed his servants to dig a well.
Ad quem locum cum venissent de Geraris Abimelech,
When Abimelech, and Ahuzzath, his friend,
and Phicol, the leader of the military,
had arrived from Gerar to that place,
and whom you have expelled from among you?”
“We saw that the Lord is with you,
Let there be an oath between us,
and let us initiate a pact,
ut non facias nobis quidquam mali,
so that you may not do us any kind of harm,
just as we have touched nothing of yours,
and have not caused any injury to you,
but with peace we released you,
sed cum pace dimisimus auctum benedictione Domini.
augmented by the blessing of the Lord.”
and after the food and drink,
dimisitque eos Isaac pacifice in locum suum.
And Isaac sent them away peacefully to their own place.
Ecce autem venerunt in ipso die servi Isaac annuntiantes ei de puteo, quem foderant, atque dicentes: Invenimus aquam.
Then, behold, on the same day the servants of Isaac came, reporting to him about a well which they had dug, and saying: “We have found water.”
et nomen urbi impositum est Bersabee,
And the name of the city was established as ‘Beersheba,’
In truth, at forty years of age, Esau took wives:
Judith, the daughter of Beeri, the Hittite,
et Basemath filiam Elon ejusdem loci:
and Basemath, the daughter of Elon, of the same place.
quæ ambæ offenderant animum Isaac et Rebeccæ.
And they both offended the mind of Isaac and Rebekah.
